title: Evaluation of the Use of an AI-Based Mobile Device App for the Presentation of Institution-Specific Antibiotic Guidelines for Empirical Antibiotic Therapy
summary:
Multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) and the simultaneously limited development of new antibiotics represent a potential threat to public health. Rational, controlled, and appropriate antibiotic use is a key component in controlling the spread of MDROs, minimizing adverse drug reactions, and maintaining the effectiveness of antimicrobial treatment regimens.

Antibiotic Stewardship (AMS) programs and interventions have been shown to reduce the incidence of infections and colonization with MDROs, as well as the incidence of Clostridioides difficile infections. The primary focus of AMS programs is the optimization of antimicrobial therapy with the goal of achieving the best possible patient outcomes. To improve rational antibiotic prescribing, AMS programs employ a variety of strategies. Among these, official recommendations advocate the development of local, institution-specific treatment guidelines (hereinafter referred to as Standard Operating Procedures [SOPs]), which should be based on national and international guidelines as well as local resistance patterns and institutional structures.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in medicine, including the field of infectious diseases. However, AI-based decision-support tools have not yet become part of routine clinical practice in Antibiotic Stewardship. Nevertheless, several studies have already investigated the potential impact of AI in AMS. Relevant aspects include not only the optimization of antimicrobial therapy through clinical decision-support systems but also improvements in efficiency through the use of AI-assisted applications.

Research Question: Does the use of an AI-based mobile application designed to facilitate access to and presentation of institutional antimicrobial guidelines improve guideline adherence in empiric antibiotic therapy?

Methodology
- Study participants: Attending physicians responsible for inpatient ward care (ward physicians).
- Study design: Longitudinal study with a two-phase assessment of empiric antibiotic therapies conducted simultaneously across multiple clinical departments.
Intervention: Use of an AI-based mobile application providing enhanced access to institutional antimicrobial guidelines.
- Outcome measure: Comparison of guideline adherence in empiric antibiotic prescribing with and without use of the AI-based application.
- The parameters are collected through regular ward rounds and review of the electronic medical records by the study team
-The app does not provide any new medical information; rather, it presents the existing in-house antimicrobial guidelines in a different format than previously used.
conditions: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Presentation Antibiotic Stewardship Guidelines

interventions.name: Documentation of empiric antibiotic therapies in four departments of the university hospital over a period of three months without, followed by three months with, the use of an AI-based app

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Physicians working on the wards participating in the evaluation who have consented to participate and are in volved in prescirbing antibiotics
Exclusion criteria:
- non-physician staff
- medical staff without consent and without prescribing authority for antibiotics
- Preoperative/perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis
- Initiation of antibiotic therapy outside the participating wards (intensive care unit, external hospitals, or antibiotic therapies started in the outpatient setting)
